This notice explains what happens to inf: This notice explains what happens to information when you use this website. It covers the contact form on the Contact page, the meeting booker on the Schedule page, and the small number of third-party requests the site makes whenever a page loads.

The contact form asks for your name, you: The contact form asks for your name, your company (optional), your email address, your telephone number (optional), your country (optional), the service you are enquiring about, and your message. Nothing else is required to send it.
The form also contains one field that a: The form also contains one field that a person never fills in and never sees. It exists only to catch automated submissions: if it has been filled, the enquiry is discarded and nothing is stored.
We use the details you send for one purp: We use the details you send for one purpose: to read your enquiry and reply to it. The email address you give is the address we answer at.

The site serves its typefaces from this: The site serves its typefaces from this website, and its placeholder photography from the Unsplash image CDN. When a page loads, your browser requests the photography directly from Unsplash, which means your IP address and basic browser details are visible to that provider.
This happens on every visit, whether or: This happens on every visit, whether or not you use a form. It is a consequence of how the site is currently built, and it is stated here rather than left unmentioned.
The meeting booker does not load Cal.com: The meeting booker does not load Cal.com code in your browser and does not embed its calendar. Your browser calls this website only; the server then calls Cal.com and Resend. Those providers receive the details needed to make the booking and send its mail, under their own privacy terms.
The company that hosts this website also: The company that hosts this website also keeps standard server logs — such as IP address and requested page — as part of running the server. The host and its retention period have not been chosen yet.
A retention period has not been set yet: A retention period has not been set yet for enquiries, and we have not yet confirmed the retention settings of the Cal.com account that stores bookings. Until both are decided, treat this as undecided rather than as a promise. This notice will be updated to state the periods before the site is published.
To reserve a meeting, the booker asks fo: To reserve a meeting, the booker asks for your name, email address, company and phone number (both optional after the first two), the purpose of the meeting, and your timezone. It also records the date and time you choose.
That information is sent to this website: That information is sent to this website’s own server, which passes the booking details to Cal.com so the meeting exists on the company calendar, and to Resend so the confirmation, notification and any reminder can be delivered. The private credentials for those services are never sent to your browser.
The confirmation screen shows a signed l: The confirmation screen shows a signed link that lets you reschedule or cancel that one booking without signing in, and our branded emails include the same link when they are enabled. Otherwise our scheduling provider’s confirmation carries its own management links. Our link is tied to both the booking and the email address it was issued for; changing either makes it invalid.
What you are entitled to ask us to do wi: What you are entitled to ask us to do with your information depends on where you live; different jurisdictions grant different rights. We have not yet confirmed which regime applies to Afghan Futian.
